issue.silent.title: Not heard from
issue.late.title: Stopped reporting
issue.late.detail: No messages for {duration}. It should report at least every {every}.
issue.unidentified.title: Never identified
issue.unidentified.detail: Interview didn't complete, so the model is unknown. Try re-pairing it.
issue.frozen.title: Reading not changing
issue.frozen.detail: {reading} stuck at {value} for {duration} across {n} reports. Try Reconfigure.
issue.weak_signal.title: Weak signal
issue.signal_drop.title: Signal dropping
issue.signal_drop.detail: Link quality {lqi} today vs {prev} over the previous week.
issue.battery_low.title: Low battery
issue.battery_low_reported.title: Low battery
issue.battery_soon.title: Battery running down

issue.battery_soon.detail.one: Expected to reach 10% in about {n} day.
issue.battery_soon.detail.other: Expected to reach 10% in about {n} days.

issue.update.title: Firmware update available
issue.flapping.title: Keeps dropping out
issue.flapping.detail: In the last 24 h it {what}. Usually a weak or unstable link, a failing power supply, or a router nearby that keeps restarting.
issue.chatty_high.title: Very chatty
issue.chatty_high.detail: About {rate} messages an hour (one every {every} s) over the last 6 h. That much traffic slows the whole mesh. Raise its reporting interval or set debounce/throttle for it in Zigbee2MQTT.
issue.chatty_rise.title: Chattier than usual
issue.chatty_rise.detail: About {rate} messages an hour over the last 6 h, against its usual {usual}. Something changed: a stuck sensor, a reporting setting, or an automation sending commands in a loop.
issue.battery_drain.title: Battery draining fast
issue.battery_drain.detail: Dropped {dropped}% in the last {n} days, about {factor}× its usual rate of {usual_rate}% a day. Often a weak link to its router (it keeps retrying), or a sensor stuck reporting.
issue.battery_drain_via.title: Battery draining fast
issue.battery_drain_via.detail: Dropped {dropped}% in the last {n} days, about {factor}× its usual rate of {usual_rate}% a day. It connects through {parent} (LQI {lqi}). Often a weak link to its router (it keeps retrying), or a sensor stuck reporting.
issue.binding_lost.title: Binding lost

issue.binding_lost.detail.one: {n} binding gone since {since}: {names}. Re-create it in Zigbee2MQTT on the device's Bind tab.
issue.binding_lost.detail.other: {n} bindings gone since {since}: {names}. Re-create it in Zigbee2MQTT on the device's Bind tab.

issue.binding_lost_coordinator.title: Binding lost

issue.binding_lost_coordinator.detail.one: {n} binding gone since {since}: {names}. Reconfigure re-creates the reporting bindings to the coordinator.
issue.binding_lost_coordinator.detail.other: {n} bindings gone since {since}: {names}. Reconfigure re-creates the reporting bindings to the coordinator.

issue.single_point.title: Single point of failure

issue.single_point.detail.one: In the last routing scan it was the only path to the coordinator for {n} router ({names}){extra}. If it loses power they have to find another way in. Another router between them and the rest of the mesh removes the risk.
issue.single_point.detail.other: In the last routing scan it was the only path to the coordinator for {n} routers ({names}){extra}. If it loses power they have to find another way in. Another router between them and the rest of the mesh removes the risk.

issue.router_hopping.title: Changes router often
issue.replacement.title: Possible replacement
issue.replacement.detail: Has the same name as removed device {name} ({ieee}). Link them to carry over history.
issue.network_offline.title: Zigbee2MQTT offline
issue.network_offline.detail: Not responding for {duration}. Every device on this network is unreachable. Check the coordinator's power and network connection.
issue.router_offline.title: Router offline

issue.router_offline.detail.one: 1 device that routes through it is offline too: {names}. Check its power first.
issue.router_offline.detail.other: {n} devices that route through it are offline too: {names}. Check its power first.

issue.restart_required.title: Restart needed
issue.restart_required.detail: Zigbee2MQTT says it needs a restart to apply a settings change.
issue.pairing_open.title: Pairing open
issue.pairing_open.mqtt: opened from Home Assistant or an automation
issue.backup_missing.title: Coordinator backup
issue.backup_missing.detail: There's no coordinator_backup.json in its data folder. Without it, a replacement coordinator can't take over the network and every device must be re-paired.
issue.backup_unreadable.title: Coordinator backup
issue.backup_no_key.title: Coordinator backup
issue.backup_no_key.detail: coordinator_backup.json has no network key, so it can't restore the network.
issue.backup_channel.title: Coordinator backup
issue.backup_channel.detail: The backup is for channel {backup} but the network runs on channel {network}. It's from an older network and wouldn't restore this one.
issue.backup_pan.title: Coordinator backup
issue.backup_pan.detail: The backup's PAN ID ({backup}) doesn't match the running network ({network}). It's from an older network and wouldn't restore this one.
issue.backup_old.title: Coordinator backup

issue.backup_old.detail.one: The last coordinator backup is {n} day old. Zigbee2MQTT normally refreshes it at least daily, so writing it may be failing.
issue.backup_old.detail.other: The last coordinator backup is {n} days old. Zigbee2MQTT normally refreshes it at least daily, so writing it may be failing.

issue.signal_dip.title: Daily signal dip

issue.signal_dip.detail.one: Signal drops across {n} device most {period}, {start}–{end}. Something switches on then: Wi-Fi traffic on an overlapping channel, a microwave, or a USB 3 device near the coordinator.
issue.signal_dip.detail.other: Signal drops across {n} devices most {period}, {start}–{end}. Something switches on then: Wi-Fi traffic on an overlapping channel, a microwave, or a USB 3 device near the coordinator.

check.offline.label: Offline
check.offline.description: Zigbee2MQTT has marked the device unavailable, and it stays that way for longer than the offline alert delay.
check.silent.label: Not heard from
check.silent.description: No messages for 2 days from a device without availability reporting.
check.late.label: Stopped reporting
check.late.description: No messages for longer than the device's own report interval, set on its Health tab.
check.frozen.label: Frozen reading
check.frozen.description: Temperature, humidity, pressure or air quality hasn't changed while the device keeps reporting.
check.battery_low.label: Low battery
check.battery_low.description: Battery at or below the battery threshold, or the device reports low battery.
check.battery_soon.label: Battery running down
check.battery_soon.description: Battery expected to reach 10% within 45 days.
check.weak_signal.label: Weak signal
check.weak_signal.description: Average link quality below 30 over the last 24 hours.
check.signal_drop.label: Signal dropping
check.signal_drop.description: Link quality today is well below the previous week.
check.unidentified.label: Unidentified device
check.unidentified.description: A device joined but its interview never completed.
check.update.label: Firmware update
check.update.description: Zigbee2MQTT reports a firmware update is available.
check.replacement.label: Possible replacement
check.replacement.description: An active device has the same name as a removed one.
check.network_offline.label: Network offline
check.network_offline.description: Zigbee2MQTT or its coordinator stops responding for 2 minutes.
check.restart_required.label: Restart needed
check.restart_required.description: Zigbee2MQTT says it needs a restart to apply settings.
check.pairing_open.label: Pairing left open
check.pairing_open.description: Pairing (permit join) stays open for 10 minutes, or something other than the Zigbee Tracker opened it.
check.flapping.label: Flapping
check.flapping.description: Drops offline 4 or more times in 24 hours, or leaves the network twice, even if each drop is short.
check.chatty.label: Chatty device
check.chatty.description: Sends more messages an hour than the chatty threshold, or 5 times its usual rate. Floods the mesh for everyone.
check.battery_drain.label: Battery draining fast
check.battery_drain.description: Battery fell at least 3 times faster over the last 14 days than its usual rate. Often a weak link to its router.
check.binding_lost.label: Binding lost
check.binding_lost.description: A binding (device to device, group or coordinator reporting) disappeared and hasn't come back after 10 minutes.
check.single_point.label: Single point of failure
check.single_point.description: A router that is the only path to the coordinator for other routers in the last routing scan.
check.router_hopping.label: Changes router often
check.router_hopping.description: An end device whose parent router changed 3 or more times in the routing scans of the last 7 days. Usually a weak link or a router that keeps dropping.
check.coordinator_backup.label: Coordinator backup
check.coordinator_backup.description: Zigbee2MQTT's coordinator_backup.json is missing, more than 3 days old, or doesn't match the running network.
check.signal_dip.label: Daily signal dip
check.signal_dip.description: Link quality drops across a network at the same 1 to 4 hours on at least 4 of the last 7 days.
check.joined.label: Device joined
check.joined.description: A device joins one of your networks.
check.left.label: Device left
check.left.description: A device leaves one of your networks.
check.interview_failed.label: Interview failed
check.interview_failed.description: A newly joined device couldn't be identified.
coord.backup_not_found: Data folder not inside /config, can't check
coord.title: Coordinators
coord.subtitle: Zigbee2MQTT and coordinator status for each network
radio.finding.overlap: {net} network (Zigbee channel {channel}, {mhz} MHz) overlaps Wi-Fi channel {wifi}. The easiest fix is moving your Wi-Fi to channel {best} in the router settings. Changing the Zigbee channel means re-pairing every device.
radio.finding.beside: {net} network (Zigbee channel {channel}) sits just beside Wi-Fi channel {wifi}. Usually fine, but busy Wi-Fi can still cause occasional drops.
radio.finding.shared: {nets} both use Zigbee channel {channel}. Separate networks on one channel share its airtime, which matters if their coordinators or devices are within range of each other. If one of them has dropouts, moving the smaller network to channel {best} would separate them. That needs every device on it re-paired, so only do it if there's a real problem.
radio.finding.clear: No overlap: your Zigbee channels are clear of the Wi-Fi channels you've entered.
radio.finding.clear_no_wifi: No overlap: your Zigbee channels are clear of the Wi-Fi channels you've entered (add your Wi-Fi channels in Settings to check them too).
radio.title: Radio channels
radio.subtitle: Zigbee channels {zigbee} · Wi-Fi {wifi}

radio.hours_title.one: Average link quality by hour, last 7 days · {n} device
radio.hours_title.other: Average link quality by hour, last 7 days · {n} devices

shop.title: Batteries to buy
shop.subtitle: {total} for devices expected to run low within 60 days
map.help: Drag dots to rearrange, drag the background to pan and scroll to zoom. Click a group in the legend to show only those devices. Solid lines show which router each battery device uses, dashed lines link routers. Colour shows link quality.
map.no_data_text: Run a routing scan to see which router each device connects through. It also runs nightly.
map.older_scan: Older scan. Advice below is for the latest scan.
map.history_builds: Scan history builds up from here, one scan a night, so you can compare before and after a change.
map.diff_none: No devices changed router and no link changed by 25 or more.
map.help_floor: Devices are grouped by Home Assistant floor and area. Solid lines show which router each battery device uses, dashed lines show each router's strongest link towards the coordinator. Colour shows link quality. Select a device to highlight its links.
map.likely_route_tip: Inferred from the scan: the router's strongest link towards the coordinator

map.fp_weak_via.one: Its only link is weak, via {name}

map.fp_likely_lqi: Likely route, inferred from the scan · LQI {lqi}
advice.better_router: {device} connects through {parent} with a weak link (LQI {lqi}), but {better} hears it much better (LQI {better_lqi}). Power-cycle {name} or press its button a few times near {better_name} so it picks the stronger router.
advice.weak_link: {device} connects through {parent} with a weak link (LQI {lqi}).
advice.same_room_router: {router} is a router in the same room, so re-pairing through it should give a much stronger connection.
advice.no_router_in: There's no router in {area}. Add a mains-powered Zigbee plug or switch nearby, then move it to that router.
advice.no_router_room: There's no router in its room. Add a mains-powered Zigbee plug or switch nearby, then move it to that router.
advice.weak_router: Router {router} only has weak links to the rest of the mesh (best LQI {lqi}). Devices that route through it suffer too. Move it closer, or add another router between it and the rest of the network.
advice.overloaded: {router} is carrying {n} battery devices directly. Adding a router or two nearby spreads the load and makes the network more resilient.
advice.room_no_router: {area} has {n} battery devices but no router. A mains-powered Zigbee smart plug in {area} would give them a closer, stronger connection.

advice.room_no_router_weak.one: {area} has {n} battery devices but no router, and {weak} of them has below-average links. A mains-powered Zigbee smart plug in {area} would give them a closer, stronger connection.
advice.room_no_router_weak.other: {area} has {n} battery devices but no router, and {weak} of them have below-average links. A mains-powered Zigbee smart plug in {area} would give them a closer, stronger connection.

advice.spof.one: {router} is the only path to the coordinator for {n} router ({names})
advice.spof.other: {router} is the only path to the coordinator for {n} routers ({names})

advice.spof_children.one: It also carries {n} battery device directly.
advice.spof_children.other: It also carries {n} battery devices directly.

advice.spof_fix: If it loses power, all of them have to find another way in. A router placed between them and the rest of the mesh gives a second path.

advice.missing.one: {n} active device wasn't in the scan: {names}. Sleepy battery devices often miss scans. If one keeps missing, check its signal.
advice.missing.other: {n} active devices weren't in the scan: {names}. Sleepy battery devices often miss scans. If one keeps missing, check its signal.

advice.none: No problems found. Every device has a reasonable link and no router is overloaded.
activity.empty_text: Joins, leaves, renames, removals, battery changes and online/offline changes appear here.

event.detail.back: Back in the Z2M device list
event.detail.gone: Gone from the Z2M device list
event.detail.repaired: Rejoined while pairing was open only through {via}
timing.title: When this device alerts
timing.not_tracked_device: Zigbee2MQTT availability is off for this device
timing.hint: Change the Zigbee2MQTT timeout in Zigbee2MQTT: Settings → Availability for all devices, or availability → timeout under one device in its configuration.yaml.
timing.hint_off: Turn on Availability in Zigbee2MQTT's settings to get Offline alerts for this device.
dhealth.no_outages_no_avail: No outages recorded (Z2M availability isn't reporting this device).
dhealth.no_readings: No temperature, humidity, pressure or air-quality readings to watch.

report.desc: Alerts when the device sends nothing for this long, even if Zigbee2MQTT still shows it online.
report.usual: Usually one message every {gap}. Set it a little above that.
report.range: Enter a time from 30 seconds to 7 days

bulk.desc.one: Set on {n} device. Change one device on its Health tab, or many at once here.
bulk.desc.other: Set on {n} devices. Change one device on its Health tab, or many at once here.

bulk.title: Expected reporting for many devices

bulk.pick_group: Pick mains devices, battery devices or both.

bulk.turned_off.one: Expected reporting turned off for {n} device
bulk.turned_off.other: Expected reporting turned off for {n} devices

traffic.counting: Message counts start from the last app update. Nothing received from this device since then.

bindings.restore_text.other: Asks Zigbee2MQTT to re-create these bindings on {name}:

bindings.restore_time: It can take up to a minute per binding.
bindings.restore_battery: This device runs on battery and may be asleep. Press a button on the device to wake it first, then confirm.
battery.no_estimate: Not enough history for an estimate yet
battery.from_library: suggested by the Battery Notes library
battery.records_bn: Records a new battery for {name} and updates Battery Notes.
battery.remove_text: Removes it from the tracker's history only. Battery Notes isn't changed.
history.not_linked: Not linked to any other device.
history.link_removed: Link a removed device this replaces…

hops.none.one: Not in any routing scan in the last {n} day.
hops.none.other: Not in any routing scan in the last {n} days.

hops.advice: A mains-powered router close to it gives it one steady route.
asset.title: Asset details
asset.note_placeholder: What is this device, where is it, why was it removed?
reconfigure.title: Reconfigure {name}?
reconfigure.text1: Zigbee2MQTT sends the binding and reporting setup to the device again. Names, settings and history aren't changed.
reconfigure.text2: Use it when a device stops updating a value. It can take up to 40 seconds.
reconfigure.offline: This device is offline (last heard {when}), so it probably won't respond. Check it has power first.
reconfigure.battery: This device runs on battery and may be asleep. Press its button just before you confirm.
mute.title: Ignore this alert?
mute.text: Stops flagging this problem for {name}. Other devices aren't affected.
rename.text: Changes the name in Zigbee2MQTT and Home Assistant together, including entity IDs.
rename.no_areas: Areas couldn't be loaded from Home Assistant.
ota.title: Update {name}?
ota.text1: Installs firmware {latest} (currently {installed}). It usually takes 10 to 60 minutes, and the device may not respond while it updates.
ota.text2: Keep it powered and in range. Battery devices need to stay awake, so press their button if the update doesn't start.
ota.reason.not_active: Device is not active in Zigbee2MQTT
ota.never_checked: Not checked by the tracker yet
ota.all_up_to_date: All firmware is up to date
ota.nothing_text: Zigbee2MQTT hasn't reported any firmware updates. Use Check now to ask every device.
ota.overnight_desc: Installs available updates in this window, one device at a time. A failed update is tried once more the next night.
ota.min_battery_desc: Battery devices below this level are skipped. Use Update anyway to override.
ota.choose_times: Choose a start and end time

ota.checking_n.one: Checking {n} device. Sleeping battery devices may not answer.
ota.checking_n.other: Checking {n} devices. Sleeping battery devices may not answer.

ota.update_all_text: Devices are updated one at a time. Each usually takes 10 to 60 minutes and may not respond while it updates.
ota.low_battery_warn: {reason}. If the battery runs out during the update, the device may need to be paired again.
ota.queued_after: Queued. It starts after the current update.
forget.title: Forget {name}?
forget.text: This permanently deletes the device's history from the tracker.
forget.still_in_z2m: It's still in Zigbee2MQTT, so it will reappear straight away with an empty history.
restore.title: Restore from backup?
restore.text: Replaces the tracker's entire history with {file}. Anything recorded since that backup is lost.
pair.choose_router: Choose the router to move it to
pair.open_move: Pairing open through the chosen router. Put {name} into pairing mode now.
pair.open_new: Pairing is open. Put the device in pairing mode now.
pair.rejoined_text: {name} rejoined while pairing was open only through {via}.
pair.rejoined_hint: Its name, history and Home Assistant entities are unchanged. Run a routing scan in a few minutes to confirm the new connection on the map.
pair.how: Usually that means holding its button for about 5 seconds until the light flashes. See {docs}. Keep it close to the router.
pair.move_explain: Battery devices pick their own router, so they can't be reassigned directly. Instead, pairing opens {only} and you re-pair {name}. Its name, history and Home Assistant entities stay the same.
pair.only_chosen: only through the router you choose
pair.open_on: Pairing is open on the {net} network. Put your device into pairing mode now.
pair.open_on_via: Pairing is open on the {net} network, only through {via}. Put your device into pairing mode now.
pair.new_hint: Choose a router near where the new device will live, or leave it on any device. Then reset the device or hold its pairing button.
pair.interviewing: Interviewing… keep it awake and close by
pair.waiting_join: Waiting for a device to join…
pair.title: Pair a new device
pair.move_subtitle: Re-pair it through a router you choose
pair.subtitle: Opens pairing, then helps you set up what joins
snack.linked_carried: Linked. History, notes and asset details carried over
snack.scan_started: Routing scan started. It takes a few minutes.
snack.import_done: Import done: {devices} new devices, {events} new events
settings.alerts_off_text: Nothing is sent. Your choices below are kept for when you turn them back on.
settings.ha_notifications_desc: Shows in the notification panel and clears itself when fixed
settings.weekly_desc: One message a week: what needs attention, batteries to buy, new and removed devices.
settings.weekly_send_desc: Uses your notification settings above, plus the {event} event
settings.checks_desc: Off stops checking. Show in Health lists it only. Show and notify also sends an alert.
settings.offline_for_desc: Extra wait after Zigbee2MQTT marks a device offline. Zigbee2MQTT only does that after its own timeout: 10 min for mains devices and 25 h for battery devices by default. So with 60 here, a mains device alerts about 70 min after its last message.
settings.frozen_for_desc: How long a reading can stay identical while the device keeps reporting
settings.battery_at_desc: Battery level at or below which a device is flagged
settings.chatty_above_desc: Messages an hour, averaged over 6 hours, before a device counts as chatty
settings.routing_scan_desc: Maps which router each device connects through. Adds network traffic for a few minutes.
settings.wifi_desc: Used to check your Zigbee channels for overlap. Your router's Wi-Fi settings show the channel, e.g. 1, 6 or 11.
settings.entities_desc: {n} published. Needs attention, Reading frozen, Reconfigure and Battery replaced are enabled. Signal, uptime, battery days left, battery type and Connected via are added disabled.
settings.language_desc: Automatic follows your Home Assistant profile. Saved in this browser.
settings.import_desc: Re-scan Z2M databases, backups, logs and HA registries for old devices and names
settings.backup_desc: Download the tracker's full history, or restore it from a backup file. Separate from HA backups.
settings.export_desc: Every device with hardware, battery and asset details as CSV
settings.networks_desc: {topics}. Add networks in the app's Configuration tab.
settings.details_desc: Side panel next to the list on wide screens, or a pop-up dialog. Phones always use the dialog.
settings.not_persisted: Applied, but couldn't save to the app configuration. It resets on restart.
settings.layout_pane: Details open in a side panel
trends.lqi_empty: Not enough link quality readings in this range yet.
trends.battery_empty: Not enough battery readings in this range yet. The device reports battery about once a day.
trends.estimate_needs: The battery estimate needs at least two weeks of falling readings since the last battery change.
replace.title: Replace {name}
replace.step.name: Name
replace.hint.name: Renamed in Zigbee2MQTT. Home Assistant entity IDs follow the name, so they stay the same once the old entities are gone.
replace.hint.no_area: The old device had no area.
replace.hint.other_network: The new device is on another network, so bindings can't be copied.
replace.hint.bindings: Re-created on the new device. Links to the coordinator are set up by Zigbee2MQTT itself.
replace.hint.battery: Off by default: a new device comes with a fresh battery.
replace.hint.remove: Force remove from Zigbee2MQTT. Its history here is kept.
replace.carried.name: name
replace.intro: Pair the new device first, then choose it here. The new device takes over {name}'s name, area and setup. Its history starts where this one ended.
replace.no_others: There are no other devices to choose from.
replace.no_new: No new unnamed devices joined in the last 7 days. Pair the new device, or show all devices.
replace.choose: Choose what the new device takes over from {name}.
replace.clash: {name} is still in Zigbee2MQTT, which won't allow two devices with the same name. Also remove the old device, or the rename will fail.
replace.linked_note: Both histories are linked either way, so each logbook points to the other.
replace.applying_text: This can take up to a minute. Keep this window open.
replace.partly_text: Some steps didn't work. The rest were applied.
replace.battery_warn: {name} runs on battery and may be asleep. Press its button just before you apply, or the bindings may fail.
more.critical_desc: Offline alert after {minutes} min instead of {normal}. High-priority phone alerts that ignore quiet hours.
settings.critical_offline_for_desc: The same for devices marked critical on their Info tab
settings.quiet_desc: Hold alerts and send one summary when quiet hours end
issue.z2m_memory.title: Zigbee2MQTT memory climbing
issue.z2m_memory.detail: Memory up {percent} % in {days} days. Restarting Zigbee2MQTT frees it; if it keeps climbing, check its log for an extension or converter that leaks.
check.z2m_memory.label: Zigbee2MQTT memory
check.z2m_memory.description: Zigbee2MQTT's own memory use grew more than 50% over the last 7 days. Needs Zigbee2MQTT 2.5 or newer.
coord.health_off: No health data from Zigbee2MQTT yet. It needs version 2.5 or newer, and sends every 10 minutes by default (Settings → Settings → Health → Interval).
issue.group_member_offline.title: Group members offline
check.group_member_offline.label: Group members offline
check.group_member_offline.description: A Zigbee2MQTT group has members that have been offline for longer than the offline threshold.
groups.title: Groups

groups.subtitle_problems.one: {n} Zigbee2MQTT group, {bad} with members to check
groups.subtitle_problems.other: {n} Zigbee2MQTT groups, {bad} with members to check
